80_marg1492: The elder, to the elect lady. This is proper, since some doubt whether these two epistles are of John the apostle. But because they are like the first both in words and in a like assertion of faith and charity against heretics, they are proved to be of the apostle, not of John the presbyter. He writes to a certain Babylonian woman, who was called by her proper name Electa, admonishing her and her children not to depart from their purpose of faith because of the heretics. By this elect lady is signified the universal mother, the Church.
80_marg1493: By her children are meant the lesser ones begotten of the Church in faith. He writes, therefore, to the universal Church, that the perfection of faith is not outside charity, and he detests the heretics who divide Jesus Christ.
